open_obligations.what_is_open: Show that every intervention signature outside the saturated real-radical ideal is nonzero at a strictly positive rational table satisfying all bit-one equalities and all bit-zero inequalities, with coordinate height at most the declared certificate bound.
open_obligations.obstruction: Real-radical nonmembership can be witnessed on an equality component disjoint from the positive exact-oracle chamber containing the supplied rational feasibility point. Saturation excludes zero factors but neither selects signs nor guarantees a rational point on the separating component.
open_obligations.attempted: The real-variety evaluation argument proves the converse. Rational approximation fails because it need not preserve the conditional-independence equations. The established rational-grid chart lemma gives a finite rational separator whenever a rational open-box chart with nonzero pulled-back signature is available, but the frozen hypotheses supply neither such a chart on every detected component nor the advertised global height bound.
open_obligations.partial_result: The implication from membership to equality is completely established by \(\mathrm{lem{:}equality\text{-}branch\text{-}soundness}\): if \(F_{D,y}\in K_{\mathcal I}\), then \(T_{D,y}(p)=T_{D_0,y}(p)\) for every \(p\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\). In the reverse direction, \(\mathrm{lem{:}rational\text{-}grid\text{-}separator\text{-}on\text{-}chart}\) proves the constructive implication on any rational open-box chart whose pullback of \(F_{D,y}\) is nonzero. If the numerator of that pullback has degree at most \(e\) on a \(k\)-dimensional chart, a grid of at most \((e+1)^k\) rational points contains a strictly positive rational exact-oracle separator. The remaining step is precisely to prove that such a chart exists whenever \(F_{D,y}\notin K_{\mathcal I}\), and that the induced coordinate height is at most \(B_{\mathrm{cert}}\).

open_obligations.what_is_open: Prove that every nonzero-normal-form branch contains a strictly positive rational exact-oracle separator within the declared finite height bound.
open_obligations.obstruction: The branch termination claim is exactly the unresolved forward implication of the rational-positive separation theorem; a nonzero real-radical remainder alone does not ensure a bounded rational separator in the required sign chamber.
open_obligations.attempted: Equality-branch soundness, exact candidate checking, the search-cardinality bound, and soundness of every returned separator are established separately. These arguments do not force a qualifying table for an arbitrary nonzero branch, because saturation does not select the positive exact-oracle chamber and supplies no rational-point height bound.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The equality output and every returned separator are sound by \(\mathrm{lem{:}equality\text{-}branch\text{-}soundness}\) and \(\mathrm{lem{:}bounded\text{-}search\text{-}certificate\text{-}soundness}\). The latter also proves that the prescribed rational search has at most
\[
2^{2m(B_{\mathrm{cert}}+1)}
\]
candidate descriptions. Each candidate is checked exactly for positivity, normalization, all bit-one equalities, all bit-zero inequalities, and a failed cross-signature. Hence, conditional on the existence of a separating table of coordinate bit length at most \(B_{\mathrm{cert}}\), the nonzero-normal-form branch terminates within the displayed bound and returns two represented DAGs with distinct intervention vectors. What is not established is that every nonzero-normal-form branch contains such a bounded rational table; exhaustion of the finite list therefore need not produce either advertised certificate under the frozen hypotheses alone.
